columns.comment: What the consent governs. third_party_sharing = disclosure of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising (CCPA/CPRA do-not-SHARE); data_sale = disclosure for monetary or other valuable consideration (CCPA/CPRA do-not-SELL) - the two are legally distinct opt-outs (the mandated link reads Do Not Sell or Share), so they are separate types, not one. Allowed values: marketing_email, marketing_sms, marketing_phone, marketing_postal, data_processing, third_party_sharing, data_sale, profiling, cookies.

columns.comment: Current decision. Allowed values: granted, withdrawn, pending, expired.
columns.name: consent_status

columns.comment: Lawful basis for processing. Allowed values: consent, contract, legitimate_interest, legal_obligation, vital_interest, public_task.

columns.comment: Region/law scope this decision applies under. May be an ISO 3166-1 country (GB), an ISO 3166-2 subdivision (US-CA), or a reserved regional code (EU) — not alpha-2-only, since regulatory scope does not map cleanly to countries. Lets one customer hold different consent per jurisdiction (GDPR vs CCPA/CPRA). NULL = global/unspecified.
columns.name: jurisdiction_code

columns.comment: Operational do-not-activate overlay for this consent scope. TRUE = suppress activation on this purpose x channel even when consent_status is granted (suppression OVERRIDES consent). Distinct from withdrawal (consent_status=withdrawn is the customer revoking permission; suppression is an operational/legal do-not-contact signal, e.g. hard bounce or a direct-marketing objection). NULL/FALSE = not suppressed.
columns.name: suppression_indicator

columns.comment: Why this scope is suppressed (set only when suppression_indicator is TRUE). Two scopes: CHANNEL-level reasons block only this consent scope (unsubscribe, hard_bounce, spam_complaint, list_hygiene); PERSON-level reasons block every plane for the profile (deceased, fraud, do_not_contact, legal_objection) via the shared UCV gold_person_do_not_target_current view, which both the owned activation gate and any paid/non-owned plane consult (ADR 0028). Allowed values: unsubscribe, hard_bounce, spam_complaint, legal_objection, deceased, fraud, do_not_contact, list_hygiene.

columns.comment: Distinct baskets (orders) in the window — the support denominator.

columns.name: is_mirrored_pair

tables.comment: Rules-based product affinity: "frequently bought together" association rules (support / confidence / lift) computed by MARKET BASKET ANALYSIS over the customer-attributed order fact (customer_order_line), for MULTIPLE TRAILING WINDOWS. One row per DIRECTED product pair × time_window (A -> B): support and lift are symmetric, confidence is directional, so both A->B and B->A are emitted. Built entirely on the BASE dimensional model — no ML, no stored affinity table, no synthetic producer: the durable product_id lives on customer_order_line, and `product` is read (current version) only for display labels (name / category / brand).
tables.name: gold_product_affinity_pairwise

tables.comment: Per-agent performance scorecard. Attributes each session to the agents on both sides (initiating and responding), then aggregates outcome metrics per agent: how many sessions it took part in, how many completed, its success rate, and average time to completion. Joins the current a2a_agent version for role/operator/trust context. Note: this measures start -> completed (the terminal lifecycle timestamp on the session), NOT start -> acceptance event; agreement (the acceptance event) can precede completion, so this is the wider end-to-end duration, named accordingly.
tables.name: gold_a2a_agent_scorecard

tables.comment: The A2A negotiation funnel, aggregated by day x channel x product. Each session is counted once at each stage it reached, so downstream can chart initiated -> negotiated -> agreed -> completed conversion and the loss (abandoned / failed / expired) by cut. Grain: one row per (session_date, communication_channel, product_id). NOTE: product_id is nullable on a2a_session (a session need not name a primary product), so all product-less sessions for a given day x channel collapse into one row with a NULL product_id — read that NULL bucket as "no primary product", not missing data.
tables.name: gold_a2a_negotiation_funnel

tables.comment: One row per A2A session with its negotiation outcome rolled up from the append-only event log: how many steps, the first offer, the final agreed price/quantity (from the acceptance event), whether a human was escalated to, and the buyer/seller/agent context. columns.comment: Scenario: gross margin per selling day in local currency that the action takes from mapped substitutes = projected_volume_lift x store-conditional demand transfer (1 - product of (1 - affinity) over the mapped substitutes sold in the store) x affinity-weighted substitute unit margin (0 when no mapped substitute sells in the store; own unit margin when substitutes sell there but their margin is unknown). columns.comment: Durable store business key of the device that fired the loop.
columns.name: store_id

columns.comment: Durable id of the zone the observing device is installed in.
columns.name: store_zone_id

columns.comment: Durable id of the observing device whose reading breached the rule, resolved from the triggering interval version-in-effect. This is the device that CAUSED the firing.
columns.name: sensor_device_id

columns.comment: Kind of device that triggered the firing, e.g. temperature for the cold-chain excursion loop.
columns.name: device_type

columns.comment: Status of the observing device at firing time: active, inactive, failed.
columns.name: device_status

columns.comment: Durable id of the firing. Identifies the action-that-ran-against-its-triggering-observation, not merely the observation -- one breaching interval can fire several actions.
columns.name: execution_log_id

columns.comment: When the action fired (UTC). The ledger ordering key.
columns.name: triggered_at_timestamp

columns.comment: Business date of the breach that fired the loop, from the triggering interval; the firing date is the fallback when the trigger was not a canonical interval. The day-grain key for rollups.
columns.name: trading_date

columns.comment: Outcome of the firing: success, failure, pending, timeout or skipped.
columns.name: execution_status

columns.comment: Milliseconds from the breaching observation to the firing. Automation RESPONSE latency, NOT ingest latency -- do not compare it to sensor_report_interval.latency_seconds.
columns.name: latency_ms

columns.comment: fast (<= 250 ms), normal (<= 1000 ms), slow (> 1000 ms), or unknown. A responsiveness band, not a data-quality one.
columns.name: response_latency_band

columns.comment: The actual payload delivered when the action fired (JSON or string representation).
columns.name: response_payload

columns.comment: Durable id of the automation action that fired.
columns.name: automation_action_id

columns.comment: What kind of action fired: system_command, notification, webhook, ticket or log_only. One breach can fan out to several action types.
columns.name: action_type

columns.comment: The kind of thing the action targeted -- actuator, role, person or external_system. Only the actuator target carries a typed actuator FK (§A.5).
columns.name: target_entity_type

columns.comment: Durable id of the target, interpreted per target_entity_type.
columns.name: target_entity_id

columns.comment: TRUE if the action version that fired was live. A disabled action leaves its rule firing but takes no effect.
columns.name: action_is_enabled

columns.comment: Template used to generate response_payload.
columns.name: payload_template

columns.comment: Durable id of the rule whose breach fired the action.
columns.name: evaluation_rule_id

columns.comment: Human-readable rule name, e.g. an over-temperature excursion on a named device.
columns.name: rule_name

columns.comment: GS1 CBV property the rule watches, e.g. gs1:Temperature. Shared vocabulary with sensor_report_interval.report_type.
columns.name: report_type

columns.comment: The comparison applied by the rule (e.g. greater_than, less_than, inside_range).
columns.name: condition_operator

columns.comment: Operational severity of the breach: info, warning or critical.
columns.name: severity

columns.comment: The threshold the observed value was compared against, in the rule unit, AS OF the firing. DOUBLE, matching sensor_report_interval.value (§A.6).
columns.name: threshold_value_numeric

columns.comment: Upper bound for inside_range or outside_range operators, in the rule unit.
columns.name: threshold_value_upper

columns.comment: Rule time_window_seconds: the sustained-breach window that must hold before the rule fires.
columns.name: time_window_seconds

columns.comment: UN/CEFACT unit code for the rule threshold (e.g. CEL for Celsius, NUM for count).
columns.name: rule_uom_code

columns.comment: Durable id of the actuator the command hit. NULL for non-actuator actions or a retired actuator.
columns.name: actuator_capability_id

columns.comment: What the actuator was commanded to do, e.g. toggle_power. NULL for a non-actuator action such as a notification.
columns.name: command_type

columns.comment: Status of the actuator at firing time: active, inactive, failed, or unknown.
columns.name: actuator_status

columns.comment: Durable business key of the asset the actuator drives, e.g. the refrigeration unit. NULL for ambient or digital-only actuation.
columns.name: equipment_id

columns.comment: The reading interval that breached the rule, closing the loop back to the observation. NULL if the trigger was not a single canonical interval.
columns.name: sensor_report_interval_sk

columns.comment: Durable id of the interval that triggered the firing (survives across SCD2 versions).
columns.name: sensor_report_interval_id

columns.comment: The observed value that breached the rule, in breach_uom. For the cold-chain loop this is the temperature that exceeded the limit.
columns.name: breach_value

columns.comment: UN/CEFACT unit code for the breach_value (e.g. CEL for Celsius, NUM for count).
columns.name: breach_uom

columns.comment: End timestamp of the triggering canonical interval.
columns.name: interval_end_ts

columns.comment: Signed difference of breach_value from threshold_value_numeric, in the rule unit. Positive means above threshold -- how far past the limit the reading was. A cross-operator magnitude is left to the consumer.
columns.name: breach_margin

columns.comment: When the view was evaluated.
columns.name: fresh_as_of_ts

tables.comment: GRAIN: one row per realised automation firing (one execution_log row), decorated with the action that ran, the rule that fired it, the actuator it hit (when the target is a device), the observing device, and the sensor_report_interval whose reading breached the threshold. This is the consumable that makes the sense -> evaluate -> act -> log loop READ AS BUILT: it is the one row a responder, an auditor and a reliability review all read, closing the loop from the firing back to the observation that caused it.
tables.name: gold_css_automation_response

tables.comment: Post-Promotion ROI at promo x category grain. gold_promo_roi rolls this up to one row per promo. Definitions: baseline_*        : from the trailing-8 non-promoted-week mean (gold_weekly_baseline), summed over the promo window (i.e. scaled to the promo's duration). incremental_units = promoted_units - baseline_units (NOT clamped; a negative value is a real "promo lost volume" signal). incremental_margin= promoted_margin - baseline_margin, where margin = revenue - units * product.unit_cost. trade_spend       : planned_trade_spend allocated to the category by its share of the promo's scope rows (realized actuals are not modelled — see summary). roi               = incremental_margin / NULLIF(trade_spend, 0). cannibalization   : shortfall below baseline on SUBSTITUTE SKUs (same category, NOT on this promo) in the promo's stores during the window. forward_buy       : shortfall below baseline on the PROMOTED SKUs in the N fiscal weeks after the promo (pantry loading); N = forward_buy_weeks (default 2, see params CTE; keep in sync with seeds.yaml post_promo.forward_buy_weeks). net_incremental_margin = incremental_margin - cannibalization_margin - forward_buy_margin.

columns.name: gap_is_approximate

columns.comment: Attained minus target on the target measure type. Exact for fill_rate/in_stock_rate; for a cycle_service_level target it is an approximation (per-cycle probability vs the time-based in-stock rate) — see gap_is_approximate. Uses the default segment target, so read as an enterprise-default gap, not a segment-accurate one.
columns.name: service_level_gap_to_target

tables.comment: ACHIEVED service level vs TARGET, per store x category x fiscal week. Review finding A2 noted the package modeled only service-level TARGETS and never measured attainment, despite inventory_position.is_stockout / stockout_pct_day being available in core. This computes two attained measures with distinct, correctly-labelled definitions (they are NOT interchangeable): - attained_in_stock_rate = 1 - (stockout SKU-days / total SKU-days) A TIME-based measure: the share of SKU-days fully in stock. Answers "how often were we in stock", not "how much demand did we meet". - attained_fill_rate     = units_sold / (units_sold + lost_units) A true DEMAND-weighted (Type II / beta) fill rate: units met divided by units demanded, where unmet demand is the censoring-aware lost_units from lost_sales_estimate (NOT the stockout-constrained actual). This is the correct like-for-like counterpart to a fill_rate target — an earlier draft used 1 - SUM(stockout_pct_day)/SKU-days, which is a second TIME-based availability measure with no demand in the denominator, so differencing it against a Type-II target was the very A2 conflation this view exists to avoid. Ratios are computed as ratio-of-sums (not a mean of per-row rates).
tables.name: gold_service_level_attainment

tables.comment: The net-permission gate: "can I contact this customer for purpose X on channel Y?" Grain: one row per customer x purpose x channel (x jurisdiction), specifically per EVALUABLE consent decision — a row exists only where the customer holds a GATE-MAPPED consent record (the four marketing_* types plus profiling / cookies / third_party_sharing / data_sale; ADR 0028). A "never asked" customer (no consent on record) is intentionally ABSENT here (neither eligible nor consent_denied): absence means "no decision to evaluate", and an activation gate must treat unknown consent as NOT eligible (do not infer eligibility from absence). Combines the THREE distinct governed states the briefs insist must not be collapsed (principle #5): consent (legal permission), preference (soft opt-out / channel), and reachability (a valid identifier/contact for the channel).
tables.name: gold_customer_activation_eligibility_current

tables.comment: The profile-grain, CHANNEL/PURPOSE/JURISDICTION-agnostic do-not-target set: every profile carrying a PERSON-level suppression on ANY current consent scope. Person-level reasons (deceased, fraud, do_not_contact, legal_objection; a GDPR Art.21 direct-marketing objection) are absolute at the person level, so this view is the SINGLE do-not-target consult for EVERY activation plane: * the OWNED-channel gate (gold_customer_activation_eligibility_current) sources it, and * any NON-OWNED / PAID activation (retail-media / DSP / clean-room onboarding built over ACU segment_membership) that does not resolve people through the owned gate MUST anti-join it before targeting, so a person-suppressed customer cannot be uploaded to a paid destination (the cross-plane closure of ADR 0027's "blocks every channel" claim; see ADR 0028). Keyed on the durable profile_id only (no jurisdiction predicate) — matching ADR 0027's deliberate, fail-safe cross-jurisdiction propagation (over-suppress rather than risk under-suppressing a do-not-contact signal that carries legal weight). No PII is exposed (pseudonymous profile_id only).
tables.name: gold_person_do_not_target_current
